name: Freerouting v2.5.0
body:
> The continuation of Freerouting's development depends directly on the financial support of the project. If you feel that Freerouting has helped you, saved you time, or delivered value to your PCB designs, please consider supporting my work by [sponsoring me on GitHub](https://github.com/sponsors/andrasfuchs) or contributing via my [Stripe donation page](https://www.freerouting.app/donate). Every contribution directly enables me to keep dedicating time to tackling increasingly complex PCB layouts, delivering seamless, zero-install EDA integrations, and advancing routing tools for both human designers and automated AI workflows.

Freerouting v2.5.0 is the biggest jump in routing performance and stability in Freerouting's history. Over the last month, I completely overhauled post-route optimization into a deterministic engine, introduced a canonical V2 continuous scoring model, integrated copper pour and power plane awareness, eliminated false-positive DRC artifacts, and introduced native CLI binaries alongside a modern KiCad 10+ IPC extension mode.

Crucially, every improvement in this release is empirically measured and validated against PCBench, a dedicated benchmark and regression prevention harness testing 1,157 real-world open-source PCB designs.

---

## Key Performance Highlights (Compared to v2.4.1)

Across the full 1,157-board corpus under identical per-board timeout budgets:

* **Clean Boards Jumped from 30.9% to 75.0% (0 DRC Violations):** Clean board completion with zero clearance violations surged from **358 / 1,157 (30.9%)** in v2.4.1 to **868 / 1,157 (75.0%)** in v2.5.0. That is an increase of **+510 clean designs (+142% relative increase)**.
* **Fully Routed Boards Rose from 51.9% to 75.4%:** Boards completed with 100% connectivity increased from **600 / 1,157 (51.9%)** in v2.4.1 to **872 / 1,157 (75.4%)** in v2.5.0 (+272 fully routed boards).
* **Higher Overall Routing Quality:** Evaluated under Freerouting's canonical V2 continuous scoring engine, average score reached **969.2** (up from 943.9 in v2.4.1).
* **Faster Total Corpus Execution:** Total corpus runtime dropped from **3,251.0 s** down to **2,997.1 s**, delivering an overall speedup while routing significantly more traces to completion.
* **Breakthrough Progress on Routine Boards (Tier B):** On the 560 standard 2–4 layer production boards in Tier B, clean completion rose from 3.4% (19 / 560) to **61.6% (345 / 560)** — a leap of **+326 clean designs**, while fully routed boards more than doubled from 28.8% (161 / 560) to **62.1% (348 / 560)** and average score improved from 916.5 to **955.0**.
* **Substantial Complex & Multi-Layer Gains (Tier C):** On dense 6+ layer boards, clean completion more than tripled from 14.8% (18 / 122) to **49.2% (60 / 122)**, fully routed boards increased from 27.0% (33 / 122) to **50.0% (61 / 122)**, and average score improved from 891.8 to **922.1**.
* **High-Stress Diagnostic Resilience (Tier D):** On large stress boards, clean completion went from 0% (0 / 22) to **50.0% (11 / 22)** and fully routed designs rose from 18.2% (4 / 22) to **50.0% (11 / 22)**, with average score jumping from 905.4 to **961.6**.

---

## Robust Empirical Testing: The PCBench Framework

Prior to this release, evaluating autorouter improvements relied on manual spot-checks or a small handful of synthetic fixtures, making it easy for localized changes to introduce subtle regressions elsewhere.

To prevent regressions and systematically guide development, I established **PCBench**, an automated benchmark harness testing **1,157 real-world PCB designs** categorized into four difficulty tiers:

* **Tier A (453-Board Canary Gate):** Fast-solving production boards verified to solve with zero unrouted connections and zero DRC violations. Under v2.5.0, Tier A achieves a **99.8% clean completion rate (452 / 453)** and **99.8% fully routed rate (452 / 453)** with an average score of **999.8 / 1000** (up from 70.9% clean and 88.7% fully routed in v2.4.1).
* **Tier B (560 Routine Production Boards):** Standard 2–4 layer designs that present active routing, escape, and optimization challenges, giving clear empirical visibility into routing yield.
* **Tier C (122 Complex & Multi-Layer Boards):** High-density 6+ layer boards testing multi-layer fanout, plane traversal, and via optimization.
* **Tier D (22 High-Stress Boards):** Massive net-count and large surface-area boards testing spatial data structures and memory boundaries.

Full per-board logs, metrics, and comparisons are browsable in the [PCBench interactive web report](https://freerouting.org/benchmarks) and in-repo at `scripts/benchmark/results/benchmarks.md`.

### Corpus Benchmark Summary (All 1,157 Fixtures)

| Version | Fixtures | Clean (0 DRC) | Fully Routed | Timeouts | Failures | Total Time (s) | Avg. Score (V2) |
| :--- | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| **v2.4.1** | 1,157 | 358 / 1,157 (30.9%) | 600 / 1,157 (51.9%) | 78 / 1,157 (6.7%) | 0 / 1,157 (0.0%) | 3,251.0 | 943.9 |
| **v2.5.0** | **1,157** | **868 / 1,157 (75.0%)** | **872 / 1,157 (75.4%)** | **78 / 1,157 (6.7%)** | **0 / 1,157 (0.0%)** | **2,997.1** | **969.2** |

---

## Native CLI Executables (GraalVM PGO)

Starting with v2.5.0, Freerouting provides standalone, native command-line executables compiled via GraalVM Native Image with Profile-Guided Optimization (PGO) for:
* Linux x64
* macOS Apple Silicon (arm64)
* macOS Intel (x64)
* Windows x64

These native binaries eliminate the Java JRE requirement for CLI users, CI/CD runners, and EDA integrations, cutting startup overhead from several seconds down to sub-second instantaneous execution.

---

## Modern KiCad 10+ IPC Extension Mode

Freerouting v2.5.0 introduces direct Protocol Buffers IPC integration for KiCad 10+:
* **Modern Background Progress Dialog:** A native-feeling progress window with live stage updates (Fanout, Autoroute, Optimize), real-time score display, and responsive cancellation.
* **Non-Blocking Background Routing:** Routing runs in a separate process without freezing KiCad's user interface.
* **Robust Hardware Support:** Full support for non-copper mounting holes (NPTH) and planeless power nets.
* **Reliable Fallback:** Seamless fallback to the battle-tested Specctra DSN/SES pipeline if IPC is unavailable.

---

## Unified Deterministic Route Optimizer (`BatchOptimizer`)

The post-routing optimizer has been consolidated into a single canonical `BatchOptimizer` engine shared across Desktop GUI, CLI, and REST API pipelines:
* **Deterministic Execution:** Results are consistent and repeatable across runs. A strict total order comparator (`ItemRouteResult.compareTo`) with deterministic item-ID tie-breaking guarantees candidate selection is stable.
* **Guaranteed Best-Board Preservation:** The optimizer benchmarks baseline board state before pass 1. If subsequent passes fail to find an improvement or degrade quality, the best-known board is automatically restored before completion.
* **Reduced Memory Footprint:** Bounded candidate evaluation and lazy board copying significantly lower memory pressure and GC churn on large, dense designs.
* **Pre-Flight Guards & Fast Canary Exit:** The router skips fruitless optimization passes on incomplete boards, and boards that cannot improve exit within seconds via canary failure limits.

---

## Algorithmic, DRC & Geometric Advancements

* **Copper Pour & Power Plane Awareness (#152):** Full awareness of existing polygon copper pours and power planes during routing and clearance checks.
* **Planeless Power Layer Routing (#935):** Power nets on inner layers without predefined polygon pours now route traces cleanly instead of leaving pins unrouted.
* **Pre-Existing DRC Violation Categorization (#930):** Violations already present in the unrouted input PCB (such as pad overlaps or tight connector footprints) are detected, categorized, and separated from router-introduced violations, preventing the router from misjudging board legality.
* **Balanced Merge for Plane Cutouts (#928):** Thanks to a contribution by Patrick Reybaud, plane cutout subtraction in `getAwtArea` now uses balanced tree merging, providing an 8x to 51x rendering speedup on copper planes with hundreds of cutout holes.
* **Corner Clearance Validation:** Full tile-shape corner checks for edge connectors and castellated pads. Default copper-to-edge clearance is capped cleanly at 250 µm.

---

## Dual Scoring Model (V2 Continuous)

Freerouting separates routing completion from post-route copper efficiency into two independent 0–1000 scores:
* **Router Score (`V2_CONTINUOUS`):** Measures board completion and design rule legality. Finishing the second half of connections is weighted higher than the first half, penalizing clearance violations and shortfalls accurately.
* **Optimizer Score (`V2_LOWER_BOUND`):** Evaluates copper efficiency against placement-derived Manhattan minimum spanning tree lower bounds ($L_{\min}, V_{\min}, B_{\min}$).

---

## API, MCP & Agent Telemetry

* **1-Turn Composite Autorouting (`POST /v1/autoroute` & MCP `autoroute_board`):** AI coding agents and external scripts can now provision sessions, upload multi-file inputs, route, and receive multi-format exports in a single call.
* **Dual-User Attribution:** Telemetry now differentiates between GUI, CLI, REST API, and MCP pipelines, as well as Human and AI Agent actors.
* **Context-Optimized DRC Summaries:** Natural-language violation explanations with hotspot clustering and layout repair hints; `compact=true` drops raw coordinate bloat by >70% for LLMs.

---

## Breaking Changes & Deprecations

* **Removed Optimizer Strategies:** `-hr` (`hybridRatio`), and strategy values `RANDOM`, `GREEDY`, and `HYBRID` for `-us`/`-is` have been removed. Use `-us GLOBAL_OPTIMAL` with `-is SEQUENTIAL` or `-is PRIORITIZED`.
* **API Normalized Score Scale:** API `normalized_score` now outputs the 0–1000 canonical router score rather than a 0–1 fraction.
* **Flat Setting Keys:** Nested keys under `--router.autorouter.*` are preferred. Legacy flat keys (e.g. `--router.max_passes`) remain supported with deprecation warnings.

---

## What's Next

With v2.5.0 establishing an empirically verified baseline, my immediate focus turns to:
1. **Continuous Routing Improvements on Large & Complex Boards:** I am committed to continuously delivering even better results with bigger, more complicated boards, driving further gains in completion rates and routing quality on dense multi-layer layouts.
2. **KiCad IPC Real-Time Feedback & Control:** Throttled live trace canvas streaming so users see traces route directly inside KiCad in real-time, along with enhanced interactive control featuring start, pause, stop, and one-click undo operations.
3. **Retire KiCad SWIG in Favor of Zero-Install Native IPC:** In the next release, I will completely remove legacy KiCad SWIG support and transition fully to the modern KiCad IPC architecture powered by native CLI executables, completely removing the requirement for users to install Java 25.
4. **Escape & Congestion Fanout:** New escape routing algorithms tailored for high-density BGA packages and power nets.
5. **Multi-Threaded Autorouting:** Exploring concurrency in the primary maze-search expansion phase while preserving determinism, under the strict condition that it will only be integrated if it is proven to make the router objectively better and faster.

Thank you to everyone in the EDA, KiCad, and open-source hardware communities who contributed bug reports, board designs, and pull requests to help make this release possible!

name: Freerouting v2.4.1
body:
> If you would like to support the ongoing development of Freerouting, please consider [sponsoring me on GitHub](https://github.com/sponsors/andrasfuchs) or contributing via my new [Stripe donation page](https://www.freerouting.app/donate). Every contribution directly helps fund algorithm optimization, benchmark infrastructure, and open-source EDA tools.

Freerouting **v2.4.0** is one of the most substantial releases in the project's history. Following the feature work in v2.3.0, this release delivers a massive architectural modernization of the codebase, introduces the complete 1,157-fixture **PCBench** benchmark corpus, adds a native **Autodesk Fusion** integration, hardens security across every surface via a comprehensive multi-pass audit, migrates to OS-standard directory paths, and expands localization to **36 languages**.

---

### Highlights at a Glance

* **Architectural Separation of Concerns & Java 25** — The algorithmic routing core is now completely decoupled from Swing/AWT visual representation. The GUI runs on a pure presenter-renderer pipeline, enabling headless accessibility testing and a single unified routing pipeline across GUI, CLI, and REST API adapters.
* **PCBench Corpus (1,157 Fixtures)** — The complete real-world PCBench dataset is now hosted in-repo with a multi-tier benchmark taxonomy (Tiers A–D), automated regression gates, and a real-time console dashboard.
* **Native Autodesk Fusion Integration** — A modern, modular integration plugin for Autodesk Fusion Electronics (and modern Eagle exports) with micrometer resolution, clean DSN formatting, and automatic SCR script export.
* **Grok 4.6 Security Audit & Hardening** — Full remediation of over 30 audit findings: non-root Docker execution (UID `10001`), MCP local file sandboxing, SSRF guards, input payload bounds, and the removal of insecure Java `.frb` binary deserialization.
* **OS-Standard Directories (#845)** — Application configs, logs, jobs, and caches now respect platform-native locations (`AppData` on Windows, `Application Support` on macOS, and XDG on Linux).
* **36 Languages Worldwide** — Added 10 new languages (Slovak, Danish, Croatian, Norwegian Bokmål, Finnish, Slovenian, Greek, Hebrew, Catalan, Lithuanian) with 40+ standardized PCB technical terms.
* **Post-Routing Completion Summary & GUI Polish** — A clean post-routing modal with routing quality metrics, a redesigned stepper-based timeout control supporting runs up to 4 weeks, and high-DPI/text-scaling fixes (#804).

---

### 1. Codebase Modernization & Architecture (SoC)

Over the past months, I undertook an extensive refactoring effort to prepare Freerouting for long-term algorithmic research and headless automation:

* **Strict Separation of Concerns (SoC)** — The core geometric and algorithmic domains (`autoroute`, `board`, `geometry`, `drc`, `rules`) no longer carry Swing or AWT dependencies. Visual rendering is owned entirely by `gui.rendering` via lightweight metadata snapshots.
* **Universal Routing Pipeline** — Headless CLI, embedded REST API, and interactive GUI sessions now share a single, robust execution pipeline (`DefaultRoutingPipeline`), eliminating behavioral divergence between interfaces.
* **Retirement of Legacy `BatchV19`** — Removed the legacy v1.9 batch autorouter implementation, standardizing on the modern, actively-optimized routing engine.
* **Headless GUI Accessibility Tests** — Added component-level accessibility and interaction test suites (`testGui`) that run headlessly in CI without virtual framebuffers or physical displays.
* **Language & Build Modernization** — Fully upgraded to **Java 25**, **Gradle 9.7.1**, **JUnit 5**, and ArchUnit module boundary enforcement (`ModuleBoundariesArchTest`). Converted immutable data carriers to Java records, modernized switch expressions, and cleaned up legacy Hungarian notation and abbreviations (`*Algo` renamed to domain role classes, `ll`/`ur` to `lowerLeft`/`upperRight`).

---

### 2. PCBench Benchmark Suite (1,157 Fixtures)

To ensure that router optimizations translate to real-world performance without clearance regressions, I integrated the full **PCBench** benchmark corpus directly into the repository:

* **1,157 Real-World Boards** — Standardized Specctra DSN fixtures converted and version-controlled with exact geometric clearance tracking.
* **Multi-Tier Taxonomy** — Structured fixtures into Tier A (rapid smoke tests), Tier B (regression baseline), and deep stress suites with tier-aware stopping gates.
* **High-Performance Benchmark Runner** — Multi-worker parallel runner with real-time atomic JSON telemetry, in-place ANSI console dashboard, ETA estimation, and single-threaded CPU calibration scoring.
* **Authoritative Parity Baselines** — Published comprehensive golden performance metrics comparing v1.9.0, v2.2.4, v2.3.0, and v2.4.0.

---

### 3. Autodesk Fusion Electronics Integration

Freerouting now ships with a dedicated, modern integration for **Autodesk Fusion**:

* Located under `integrations/AutodeskFusion/`, replacing legacy scripts with a modern, modular ULP architecture.
* Full micrometer coordinate resolution, proper arc-to-line spacing, package keepout wire boundary stitching, and CCW polygon winding.
* Clean Specctra DSN export and automatic KiCad/Fusion `.scr` script output generation.
* Step-by-step setup documentation with environment guides and in-app setup screens.

---

### 4. Grok 4.6 Security Audit & Hardening

Following an in-depth security threat modeling and audit pass, I hardened all network-reachable and containerized surfaces:

* **Non-Root Docker Containers (AUDIT-027, AUDIT-028)** — The official Docker image now runs as unprivileged user `freerouting` (UID `10001`, GID `10001`) with dropped root capabilities.
* **MCP Sandboxing & SSRF Guards (AUDIT-003, AUDIT-014)** — Local file read/write tools in the MCP server are strictly sandboxed against OS system roots (`/etc`, `/proc`, `C:\Windows`), and target API URLs are validated against unauthorized loopback/metadata SSRF endpoints.
* **Retirement of Insecure `.frb` Serialization (AUDIT-024)** — Removed legacy Java object deserialization (`.frb` files) in favor of Specctra DSN/SES and JSON formats, eliminating arbitrary object injection risks.
* **Input Validation & DoS Protection (AUDIT-008, AUDIT-017)** — Enforced payload size caps and strict Base64 decoding limits on all job endpoints.
* **Transient Credentials & Safe Configs** — Sensitive CLI flags are redacted from logs, authorization tokens are marked transient in memory, and local configuration files enforce restricted `0600` permissions.

---

### 5. OS-Standard Directories (#845)

Freerouting no longer pollutes user home roots or random working directories with log and config files:

* **Windows:** Settings stored in `%APPDATA%\freerouting`, logs and cache in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\freerouting`.
* **macOS:** Stored in `~/Library/Application Support/freerouting` and `~/Library/Caches/freerouting`.
* **Linux:** Strictly follows the XDG Base Directory specification (`~/.config/freerouting`, `~/.local/share/freerouting`, `~/.cache/freerouting`).
* Self-hosted Docker deployments can override the entire storage root via `--user_data_path=/mnt/freerouting`.

---

### 6. Expanded Localization (36 Languages)

My automated contextual translation pipeline (powered by Gemini 3.7 and comprehensive PCB technical glossaries) has expanded Freerouting's reach to 36 languages:

* **10 New Languages:** Slovak (`sk`), Danish (`da`), Croatian (`hr`), Norwegian Bokmål (`nb`), Finnish (`fi`), Slovenian (`sl`), Greek (`el`), Hebrew (`he`), Catalan (`ca`), and Lithuanian (`lt`).
* **Terminology Standardization:** Standardized over 40 technical terms (via necking, pull-tight, keepouts, plane nets, clearance classes) across all supported locales.
* Automatic fallback to English for missing keys and CLI language selection support via the `-l` argument.

---

### 7. GUI Polish, Controls & Other Improvements

* **Post-Routing Completion Summary** — When a routing job finishes in the GUI, an informative summary modal displays the final score, routed connections, total trace length, via count, and routing time.
* **Redesigned Timeout Control** — Replaced the plain numeric field with an intuitive stepper and unit selector (seconds, minutes, hours, days, weeks), allowing routing runs up to 4 weeks (672 hours).
* **Net Class Track Widths (#796)** — Fixed an issue where edited track widths in the Net Class dialog were not persisted on blur.
* **High-DPI & Text Scaling (#804)** — Dialog windows now dynamically clamp height and enable vertical scrolling when large OS font scaling is enabled.
* **Clean Window Exit** — Cleanly dispatches daemon thread shutdown and stops internal API services on `File > Exit` or `Alt+F4`.
* **Specctra `.rules` Autoroute Settings (#848)** — Support for parsing `autoroute_settings` in `.rules` files and uploading rules directly via the REST API.
* **New Website & Support Channels** — Completely refreshed [freerouting.app](https://www.freerouting.app) design system, updated documentation, and integrated Stripe support channels.
* **Hardened Telemetry** — Enhanced BigQuery analytics with exponential backoff, retry executors, and SHA-256 tenant token anonymization.

---

### Known Limitations & Guidance

| Topic | Guidance |
|---|---|
| **KiCad Integration** | Standard Specctra DSN/SES mode remains the primary, recommended production path. |
| **Copper-to-Edge Clearance (#558)** | KiCad DSN exports omit board-edge clearance. Use `--router.copperToEdgeClearanceUm=500` (or match your KiCad design rules) to enforce proper trace back-off from board outlines. |
| **Single-Threaded Optimizer** | Multi-threaded optimizer experimentation remains disabled by default for determinism; single-threaded optimization is active and default. |

---

### Contributors

A huge thank you to everyone who contributed code, design feedback, bug reports, and translations during this release cycle, including **@26oppy**, **@mdeweerd**, **@gusbourg**, **@BanjoR**, **@physics515**, **@MrDix**, and all contributors across the EDA community!

name: Freerouting v2.3.0
body:
> If you would like to support the project, please consider [sponsoring me](https://github.com/sponsors/andrasfuchs). Even a small monthly donation is greatly appreciated!

Freerouting **v2.3.0** is a feature release focused on denser SMD routing, AI-agent integration, and a much smoother GUI — plus an experimental KiCad JSON/API path for KiCad 9+. Since v2.2.4 (May 2026) this includes a reintroduced fanout pre-pass, a dedicated MCP/A2A server, copper-to-edge clearance overrides, bend-cost support for single-sided boards, and broad localization and stability work.

### Highlights

- **SMD fanout pre-pass** — `BatchFanout` is back, with multi-layer escalation, micro-neckdown fallback, and stagnation stop so dense all-SMD boards escape pads far more reliably (#692, #730).
- **MCP + A2A** — Dedicated Model Context Protocol server (JSON-RPC, SSE, WebSocket) and public A2A agent card, usable locally or via the NPX online bridge (#696, #720, #724).
- **KiCad JSON/API mode (experimental)** — Opt-in SWIG → JSON → localhost REST path for KiCad 9+. **DSN remains the default and recommended** production workflow (#705, #765).
- **Copper-to-edge clearance** — Override board-edge clearance from CLI/settings (`--router.copperToEdgeClearanceUm=…`) as a mitigation for KiCad’s missing DSN export (#558).
- **Single-sided / bend costs** — Per-layer bend costs so single-sided fabrication constraints can be expressed in the router (#156 / #712).
- **Optimizer on by default** — Post-route optimizer enabled in default settings, with refined stop criteria.

### Routing Engine

- **Reintroduce and harden fanout** — Configurable `router.fanout` settings (passes, via diameters, pin sort order, rip-up); outer-pin prioritization; same-net via handling; escape-path length bounds (#692, #730).
- **Micro-neckdown fallback** — Failed fanout inserts can retry at a reduced width (bm05 escape ratio improved substantially in development runs).
- **Fanout stagnation stop** — Detect oscillating no-progress fanout cycles that the board-hash check alone can miss (#739, @gusbourg).
- **Opt-in `strict_drc`** — Rip connections that introduce clearance violations and restore the prior board snapshot.
- **Opt-in width necking** — Retry failed connections at `neck_width_um`.
- **Honor drill-hole-to-copper clearance** end-to-end through search and insertion.
- **Preserve trace costs across autoroute restarts** so preference settings survive pass boundaries.
- **Suppress repeated trace normalization** after an oscillation/depth cap (#741, @gusbourg).
- **SES export: snap wire endpoints** to contacted pad/via centers for better EDA round-trip (#737, @gusbourg).
- **Prevent routing on dedicated power planes**; validate plane layers on board load.
- **Handle DSN multi-boundary paths** with a safer load fallback.

### API, MCP & Automation

- **Dedicated MCP server** — Independent `mcp_server` settings (endpoints, auth, CORS, rate limits, `target_api_base_url`).
- **A2A agent card** — `GET /.well-known/agent.json` for agent discovery.
- **Local + online modes** — Embedded Java MCP (incl. stdio bridge) and `@freerouting/freerouting-mcp-server` NPX forwarder to the public API.
- **Fixed-window rate limiting** and **`X-Correlation-ID`** tracing on API and MCP requests.
- **API auth defaults hardened** — Authentication enabled by default; API binds to `127.0.0.1` by default for safer local use (disable auth explicitly for local EDA plugins).
- **Python API client** updated for the current endpoint surface.

See `docs/API/MCP.md` and `docs/API/API_v1.md`.

### KiCad Integration

- **DSN mode (default)** — Unchanged Specctra export/import; recommended for production.
- **JSON/API mode (experimental)** — Plugin dual-mode (`ROUTING_MODE_DSN` / `ROUTING_MODE_JSON`); in-repo `KiCadJsonReader`/`Writer` and REST job I/O.
- Not KiCad’s official protobuf IPC API (that remains a v2.4+ track).
- Known gap: copper-to-edge and some design-rule fields are not fully imported on the JSON/API path yet (#558).

### GUI & Usability

- Routing settings dialog redesign (units, hierarchy, pull-tight labels) (#683, @26oppy).
- Layer / object visibility upgrade, virtual layers, drill-hole rendering (#700, #715).
- Multiple net-class layer selection (#711, @26oppy).
- Drag-and-drop board loading for DSN/JSON with save confirmation (#760, @26oppy).
- DPI / multi-monitor text scaling, cursor scaling while scrolling, zoom-select rubberband, component-drag lag, middle-button pan / plane rendering speedups (#722, #744, #745, #749, #781, @26oppy).
- About / user-settings polish (#688, @26oppy).
- Faster GUI board load and plane rendering (#727, #732).

### Localization (i18n)

- Contextual LLM translation pipeline with PCB glossaries and incremental retranslation (#748, @26oppy).
- Italian support plus expanded locale coverage (glossaries for ~25 languages including Arabic, Bengali, Chinese, Czech, Dutch, French, German, Hindi, Hungarian, Indonesian, Japanese, Korean, Polish, Portuguese, Romanian, Russian, Spanish, Swedish, Thai, Turkish, Ukrainian, Vietnamese, and more).
- Missing-key fallback to English; parameterized GUI strings; English copy review.

### Architecture & Quality

- **Command pattern** for interactive GUI state (`InteractiveCommand`) and ArchUnit module-boundary enforcement (#694, #719).
- Cap **`BoardHistory`** at 30 snapshots to stop long-run memory growth (#684 / #686).
- Make **`PolylineTrace.combine()` iterative** to avoid `StackOverflowError` on long traces (#723 @physics515, #764 @MrDix) — fixes #754 / #759-class crashes.
- Guard null corners in forced-trace insertion (#751, @pascalkrijnberg).
- Thread-safe `MinAreaTree` traversal; SES orientation precision (#742 / #746).
- End-to-end benchmarking + DRC scoring infrastructure (#725).
- Optimizer enabled by default; refined stop-after-repeated-failures criteria.

### Infrastructure & Build

- Gradle wrapper **9.7.0**; project version **2.3.0**.
- Multi-platform Docker images (`linux/amd64`, `linux/arm64`) for nightly and release tags.
- Distribution script path fixes (shellcheck) (#768, @mdeweerd).
- VersionChecker always prefixes `v` (#704, @acornejo).

### Known Limitations

| Topic | Guidance |
|---|---|
| KiCad JSON/API | **Experimental** — use DSN for production work |
| [#558](https://github.com/freerouting/freerouting/issues/558) Edge clearance | DSN: set `--router.copperToEdgeClearanceUm=500` (or your KiCad value). JSON/API does not yet read KiCad’s copper-edge clearance |
| [#152](https://github.com/freerouting/freerouting/issues/152) Copper plane routing | May still introduce clearance violations on some plane nets |
| [#383](https://github.com/freerouting/freerouting/issues/383) Star ground | Deferred to v2.4 — manual lock-and-route workflow unchanged |

### Contributors

Thank you to everyone who contributed code, fixes, translations, and reviews since v2.2.4, including **@26oppy**, **@gusbourg**, **@mdeweerd**, **@MrDix**, **@physics515**, **@pascalkrijnberg**, **@acornejo**, and all issue reporters who helped shake out the fanout, SES, and crash fixes.
```

name: Freerouting v2.2.4
body:
> If you would like to support the project, please consider [sponsoring me](https://github.com/sponsors/andrasfuchs). Even a small monthly donation is greatly appreciated!
> 
> You can also fuel my passion by sharing your success stories with Freerouting - send them to info@freerouting.app, I would love to read every one of them!

This release focuses on autorouter stability, fixing several edge-case failures—including infinite loops, crashes, and copper pour connectivity issues—that occurred on complex PCB designs. Key improvements include a new board-hash stagnation check, graceful handling of deep trace normalizations, and corrected layer initialization for DSN-based routing.

### Bug Fixes & Autorouter Stability

This release focuses on robustness improvements to the autorouter, fixing several edge-case failures that could cause the router to loop indefinitely, crash, or produce incorrect scores — especially on boards with copper pours (power planes) and complex net topologies.

- **Fix layer initialisation for DSN autoroute (Issue #676)**
  Corrects a layer-setup bug in the DSN autoroute code path that could produce incorrect routing on multi-layer boards.

- **Fix `max_connections` calculation for nets**
  The number of required connections per net is now computed correctly, preventing premature routing-complete detection.

- **Normalize trace lengths to millimetres for scoring**
  Trace-length scores were previously in internal units. They are now normalised to millimetres to make the score comparable across different board scales.

- **Improve autorouter stagnation and plane-net handling**
  The autorouter now correctly identifies when no progress can be made and exits cleanly instead of running indefinitely. Plane-net items that are already connected are skipped to avoid false-work and spurious "normalisation failed" warnings.

- **Stop autorouter on repeated identical board state**
  A board-hash stagnation check (matching v1.9 behaviour) is now applied between passes. When the same board state is seen twice, the router stops and reports the result rather than looping.

- **Avoid throwing on max normalisation depth**
  `PolylineTrace.normalize()` previously threw an exception when the maximum recursion depth was reached; this was silently swallowed and logged as a "normalisation failed" warning. It now returns `false` gracefully so the outer loop continues processing remaining traces.

- **Guard divide-by-zero in `getNormalizedScore()`**
  When a board is fully routed (`maximumCount == 0`), the score denominator is zero. The guard now returns `0f` in this case, preventing `NaN` comparisons that caused the stagnation check to malfunction.

- **Check search-tree entries before polyline join**
  `PolylineTrace.combine_at_end()` now verifies that both traces have entries in the default search tree before attempting the fast merge path, preventing a `NullPointerException` in `ShapeSearchTree.merge_entries_at_end`.

- **Restore best board; deduplicate `getImpactedPoints`**
  The best-known board state is now restored at the end of a routing run when the final pass is worse. Duplicate points in `getImpactedPoints` are removed to reduce log noise.

### Improvements

- **Log settings merge at debug level**
  Settings-merge operations are now logged at `DEBUG` rather than a higher level, reducing log noise in normal operation.

- **Update benchmark messages; remove unused import**
  Minor housekeeping in the benchmarking output and code.

### Documentation

- **Clarify routing algorithm explanation in architecture docs** (contributed by @26oppy)
  The routing algorithm section in `docs/architecture.md` has been updated with a clearer explanation of the wave-expansion and A*-based approaches.

- **Document autorouter plane & loop fixes**
  `docs/issues/Issue152-copper-pour-plane-awareness.md` and `AGENTS.md` updated to reflect the fixes applied in this release.

- **Fix image link format in `developer.md`**
  Corrected a broken Markdown image link.

- **Clarify Maven Central publishing step**
  The developer documentation for publishing to Maven Central has been updated for clarity.

### Infrastructure & CI

- **Fix `ValueError: too many values to unpack` when no JRE 25 is found**
  The Python helper script that detects a local JRE 25 installation now handles the case where no matching JRE is present without raising an unhandled exception.

- **Use `NetHttpTransport` and handle SES write errors**
  HTTP transport in the Google API client is switched to `NetHttpTransport` for compatibility. SES file write errors are now caught and logged rather than silently failing.

- **Add Gemini auth checks; adjust timeouts/filters**
  The Gemini CI workflows now validate authentication before executing, with adjusted timeouts and label filters for more reliable triage runs.

- **Increase `maxSessionTurns` and tighten triage prompts**
  Gemini CLI session configuration updated for more complete automated issue triage.

- **Quote env expressions with double quotes in workflows**
  GitHub Actions workflow YAML updated to correctly quote environment variable expressions, preventing potential shell-expansion issues.

- **Update KiCad Freerouting plugin to 2.2.4**
  The bundled KiCad plugin integration under `integrations/` has been updated to reference the 2.2.4 release.

### Refactoring & Build

- **Refactor publishing setup; Javadoc/signing fixes**
  Gradle publishing configuration refactored for cleaner Maven Central artifact generation. Javadoc task and artifact signing are now correctly wired.

### New Test Coverage

- **`Issue676RoutingTest`** — Full-pass routing test for the DSN autoroute layer-initialisation fix, ensuring the reported regression does not recur.

name: Freerouting v2.2.3
body:
> If you would like to support the project, please consider [sponsoring me](https://github.com/sponsors/andrasfuchs). Even a small monthly donation is greatly appreciated!
> 
> You can also fuel my passion by sharing your success stories with Freerouting - send them to info@freerouting.app, I would love to read every one of them!

This release focuses on correctness and stability: a long-standing bug that silently broke routing on any board with more than two copper layers has been fixed, the API server is now secure by default, and a number of packaging, logging, and CI improvements have landed.

---

## Bug Fixes

- **Fixed routing failures on boards with more than 2 copper layers** (PR [#671](https://github.com/freerouting/freerouting/pull/671))  
  `RouterSettings` incorrectly hardcoded 2-layer defaults for all per-layer arrays (`isLayerActive`, preferred-direction costs, etc.). Any board with more (or fewer) layers could crash with `ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException` or silently produce wrong routing results.  
  The fix removes the incorrect assumption at its source: `DefaultSettings` no longer initialises per-layer arrays, and `DsnFileSettings` now extracts the layer count from the DSN file and seeds the arrays to the correct size. `RouterSettings.clone()` and `get_trace_cost_arr()` were also hardened against `null` arrays.  
  New `MultiLayerBoardRoutingTest` tests verify correct handling of 4-layer and 6-layer boards.  
  > Special thanks to **@thandal** and **@inktomi** who independently identified and reported this bug and provided invaluable analysis, stack traces, and test cases in PRs [#657](https://github.com/freerouting/freerouting/pull/657) and [#658](https://github.com/freerouting/freerouting/pull/658). Their work made it straightforward to trace the failure back to its root cause.

- **Fixed NPE when clicking "Autoroute" with no board loaded** (PR [#654](https://github.com/freerouting/freerouting/pull/654) by [@SAY-5](https://github.com/SAY-5))  
  The toolbar now skips the start-routing action when no input file is loaded, preventing a `NullPointerException` on `routingJob.input.format`.

- **Fixed empty Linux installer ZIP** (Issue [#652](https://github.com/freerouting/freerouting/issues/652))  
  Passing a `.ico` file to `jpackage` on Linux caused jpackage to fail silently and produce a nearly empty archive. The packaging script now uses a `.png` icon (as required by jpackage on Linux) and adds `set -e` so failures are surfaced immediately.

- **Fixed KiCad plugin failing when project path contains spaces** (Issue [#653](https://github.com/freerouting/freerouting/issues/653))  
  The KiCad integration plugin now redirects intermediate routing files to a guaranteed space-free temporary directory when the project path contains spaces, then cleans up after import.

---

## New Features & Enhancements

- **Board scoring breakdown and comparison tools**  
  Introduced `BoardScoreBreakdown` (immutable per-component scoring) and `ScoringWeightComparison` (compare two `RouterScoringSettings` against the same `BoardStatistics`) with a rich text report. Scoring setting fields were renamed to camelCase (`viaCosts`, `planeViaCosts`, `startRipupCosts`) and defaults were centralised in `DefaultSettings`.

- **Secure-by-default API server**  
  API authentication is now **enabled by default**. The server also binds to `http://127.0.0.1:37864` (localhost only) by default, eliminating unintended network exposure for local EDA plugin use. A startup warning is shown when authentication is explicitly disabled. To use Freerouting headlessly with a local EDA plugin, run:
  ```
  java -jar freerouting-executable.jar --gui.enabled=false --api_server.enabled=true --api_server.authentication.enabled=false
  ```

- **Rolling log files**  
  The log appender is now a `RollingFile` appender with a 50 MB size trigger and up to 10 compressed (`gz`) rotated files, preventing unbounded log growth on long-running instances.

- **Improved startup logging**  
  Key startup details (user-data path, log file location, settings source) are now logged at INFO level. Stale `logging.file.location` entries in `freerouting.json` (common after Docker volume changes) are detected and the file self-heals. Proactive read/write permission checks warn early when the user-data directory is not accessible.

- **Windows installer console window**  
  The Windows MSI installer now includes `--win-console` so `stdout`/`stderr` are visible in terminals, making it easier to diagnose startup and routing issues.

---

## Security

- **Log4j2 JNDI lookups disabled**  
  `log4j2.disableJndi=true` is set at the very start of `Freerouting.main()` and via `log4j2.component.properties` to prevent JNDI plugin loading entirely. `JndiLookup` and `JndiManager` classes are also excluded from the executable JAR. This reduces the attack surface and eliminates noisy WARN lines on stripped JREs.

---

## Infrastructure & CI

- **Gradle wrapper bumped to 9.5.0**  
  Includes retry and back-off settings in `gradle-wrapper.properties` and improved `gradlew.bat` exit handling.

- **Dependency and plugin upgrades**  
  Log4j, Gson, Jersey, JAXB, Jetty, Google Cloud libraries, Swagger/OpenAPI, ArchUnit, Mockito, and build plugins updated to their latest stable versions.

- **GitHub Actions CI hardening**  
  All workflow jobs now declare explicit least-privilege `permissions` blocks, `timeout-minutes` values, and `chmod +x gradlew` on Linux/macOS runners. The `create-snapshot` job dependency graph was fixed to prevent publishing broken artifacts when tests fail. Gemini CLI workflows use `GEMINI_CLI_TRUST_WORKSPACE: 'true'` consistently. Upgraded to `gradle/actions/setup-gradle@v4` and `actions/stale@v9`.

---

## Documentation

- **Architecture document** moved to `docs/architecture.md` with a refreshed Mermaid pipeline diagram, package glossary, and reading guide (PR [#664](https://github.com/freerouting/freerouting/pull/664) by [@26oppy](https://github.com/26oppy)).
- Expanded API documentation: job lifecycle, SSE streams, cancel endpoint, Swagger/OpenAPI developer tools, and step-by-step onboarding guide.
- Updated developer release instructions and dependency-update workflow docs.

---

## Localization

- Added and updated localization keys for the routing toolbar (`warn_no_input_file`, `inspect_button`, routing tooltip variants, `delete_all_tracks_button_tooltip`, `settings_button_tooltip`, `cancel_button_tooltip`, `unit_*`) across all supported locales: `ar`, `bn`, `de`, `en`, `es`, `fr`, `hi`, `ja`, `ko`, `pt`, `ru`, `zh`, `zh_tw`.

---

## Full Changelog

[v2.2.2...v2.2.3](https://github.com/freerouting/freerouting/compare/v2.2.2...v2.2.3)

name: Freerouting v2.2.2
body:
> If you would like to support the project, please consider [sponsoring me](https://github.com/sponsors/andrasfuchs). Even a small monthly donation is greatly appreciated!
> 
> You can also fuel my passion by sharing your success stories with Freerouting - send them to info@freerouting.app, I would love to read every one of them!

This release focuses on robustness improvements across the configuration system, settings I/O, and infrastructure. Key highlights include more reliable user-data path handling, flexible comma-separated list settings via CLI/environment variables, a Jetty 12 compatibility fix, and updated Docker multi-platform images.

### Changes

- **Improved user-data path handling and settings I/O** — `--user_data_path` is now created lazily on first save; `mkdirs()` failures are reported as actionable warnings instead of being silently ignored. `GlobalSettings` gains `getConfigurationFilePath()`, `resetForTesting()`, `getReleaseSafeVersion()`, and `compareVersionStrings()`; version strings are normalized (strips `-SNAPSHOT`) before comparisons and writes. Corrupt JSON files now emit a warning rather than crashing.
- **Comma-separated list settings via CLI and environment variables** — List-valued settings (e.g. `api_server.endpoints`) can now be supplied as comma-separated strings on the command line or via environment variables. `ReflectionUtil` converts them to `String[]`, trimming whitespace. CLI key/value splitting now uses `limit=2` so values containing `=` (e.g. query-string URLs) are preserved intact.
- **Jetty 12 / EE10 compatibility** — `ServletContextHandler` is now used to obtain the Jetty `Server` instance, with a fallback to the legacy `ServletContext` attribute for older versions. Missing-server events are now logged at debug rather than warn.
- **Improved SES import/export** — Replaced legacy Specctra parser/writer usage with the new `SesReader`/`SesWriter` API. Import operations now return a `SesImportSummary` (wires, vias, and errors) that is surfaced in the GUI and `RoutingJobScheduler` logs.
- **Docker image: dropped `linux/arm/v7`** — 32-bit ARM support was removed because `eclipse-temurin:25` no longer publishes an `arm/v7` image. Users running Raspberry Pi on a 32-bit OS should switch to a 64-bit OS to use the official Docker image. `linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64` (Apple Silicon, AWS Graviton, 64-bit Raspberry Pi) remain supported.
- **Comprehensive self-hosting guide** — Added `docs/self-hosting.md` covering Docker and JAR deployment, Docker Compose examples, systemd/launchd/NSSM service unit files, configuration reference, and troubleshooting steps.
- **Improved Gradle build hygiene** — `writeVersionInfo` and `writeVersionInfoV19` tasks now declare `versionId` and `buildDate` as explicit task inputs, enabling correct up-to-date checks and build caching.
- **Reduced log noise** — `ReflectionUtil` no longer emits a `WARN` when a field has no default constructor; the message is now logged at `DEBUG` level.
- **Documentation and example updates** — README, `command_line_arguments.md`, `gradle_quick_reference.md`, and `integrations.md` updated to reference 2.2.2 artifacts. Recommended JRE version bumped from 21 to 25.



**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/freerouting/freerouting/compare/v2.2.1...v2.2.2

> You can also fuel my passion by sharing your success stories with Freerouting - send them to info@freerouting.app, I would love to read every one of them!

This is a security and stability patch release. It fixes an API authentication bypass that blocked all requests when auth was disabled, hardens the default server configuration to be localhost-only with auth enabled, and resolves installer crashes caused by missing JDK modules in the bundled JRE. Browser-based EDA integrations also gain improved CORS support and a new required client-identification header.

## What's changed

-  **Fixed API auth bypass (Issue #650):** `ApiKeyValidationFilter` was rejecting requests with HTTP 401 before checking whether authentication was even enabled. The filter now skips all validation when `authentication.enabled=false`.
-  **Fixed bundled JRE crashes:** Installer scripts for Windows, Linux, and macOS now include all required JDK modules (`java.management`, `jdk.management`, `jdk.crypto.ec`, and `jdk.crypto.mscapi` on Windows). Affected call sites degrade gracefully on stripped JREs.
-  **Fixed CLI/API mode conflict:** The app no longer enters CLI mode when the API server is running alongside `--gui.enabled=false`.
-  **Hardened default settings:** API authentication is now **enabled** by default and the server binds to `http://127.0.0.1:37864` (localhost only) instead of `0.0.0.0`.
-  **New `Freerouting-Environment-Host` header:** Protected API endpoints now require this header (format: `<ToolName>/<Version>`, e.g. `KiCad/8.0`). Missing or malformed values return HTTP 400.
-  **CORS support for Freerouting headers:** `Freerouting-Profile-ID`, `Freerouting-Profile-Email`, and `Freerouting-Environment-Host` are now included in `Access-Control-Allow-Headers`, unblocking browser-based integrations (e.g. EasyEDA).

## Upgrade note for EDA plugin users

If you run Freerouting headlessly for KiCad or EasyEDA, authentication is now **on by default** — explicitly disable it and ensure your plugin sends the new header:

```
java -jar freerouting-executable.jar --gui.enabled=false --api_server.enabled=true --api_server.authentication.enabled=false
```


**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/freerouting/freerouting/compare/v2.2.0...v2.2.1

name: Freerouting v2.2.0
body:
> If you would like to support the project, please consider [sponsoring me](https://github.com/sponsors/andrasfuchs). Even a small monthly donation is greatly appreciated!
> 
> You can also fuel my passion by sharing your success stories with Freerouting - send them to info@freerouting.app, I would love to read every one of them!

## Bug Fixes

- **Max passes now respected in headless mode** (Issue #522): The `-mp` CLI argument and `maxPasses` setting were previously ignored when running without a GUI; this is now correctly enforced.
- **Clearance matrix max value** (Issue #491, #543): Fixed incorrect max value calculation in the clearance matrix, which could cause routing decisions to use wrong clearance thresholds.
- **Race condition in `StoppableThread`** (#544): Fixed a thread-safety issue that could cause unpredictable behaviour during routing cancellation.
- **Numeric padstack names quoted in session files** (#548): Padstack names and identifiers starting with a digit are now properly quoted in `.ses` output, preventing parse errors in downstream EDA tools.
- **SES file scale factor** corrected in `SesFileReader`.
- **Autorouter index validation and array resizing** fixed to prevent out-of-bounds errors on certain board configurations.
- **Final-leg traces protected from stub removal**: Traces forming the final connection leg are no longer incorrectly removed during auto-routing cleanup.
- **Degenerate geometry handling**: Null corners and degenerate shapes in `IntOctagon` and `Polyline` are now handled gracefully instead of throwing exceptions.

## New Features

- **Design Rule Checker (DRC)** (#576, #601): A comprehensive DRC engine (`DesignRulesChecker`) has been introduced. It detects:
  - Clearance violations (conductor-to-conductor, hole clearance)
  - Dangling vias and tracks
  - Unconnected net items
  - Supports JSON output via the new `-drc` CLI option and a new `GET /v1/jobs/{jobId}/drc` API endpoint.
- **Settings Merger architecture** (#606): A layered `SettingsMerger` with nine priority levels (defaults → API) now governs all router configuration, replacing the previous ad-hoc settings propagation. Environment variable overrides are supported via `EnvironmentVariablesSource`.
- **In-progress routing output** (#621): `GET /v1/jobs/{jobId}/output` can now return partial output for jobs that are still running.
- **Stagnation detection**: The autorouter now detects when routing quality has stopped improving (score-based) and terminates early, preventing wasted passes.
- **OpenAPI 3.0 / Swagger UI** (#587): The REST API is now fully documented with OpenAPI 3.0 annotations. A Swagger UI endpoint is available.
- **Modular API key validation** (#592, #619): API key checking is now provider-based (including Google Sheets as a provider), with thread-safe caching and improved error messages.
- **CORS support** for the `/v1` API endpoint.
- **SES file import** added to the CLI (`-de` argument now supports `.ses` files).
- **Specctra I/O refactoring** (#633): DSN/SES read and write logic has been moved into dedicated `io.specctra` and `io.specctra.parser` packages, decoupled from GUI and interactive code. New `DsnReader`, `DsnWriter`, `DsnMetadata`, and `DsnReadResult` types with full unit tests.

## Performance Improvements

- **Memory consumption reduced** (#549): Fixed potential memory leaks; collections in `BatchAutorouter` are now reused across passes to reduce GC pressure.
- **Object pooling for `MazeListElement`**: Reduces heap allocation churn during maze expansion.
- **Optimized maze expansion list polling**.
- **Board update events throttled** during autorouting to reduce UI overhead.
- **Optimizer logic guarded**: Optimizer code is now skipped entirely when the optimizer is disabled, avoiding unnecessary computation.
- **`maxItems` enforced during batch autorouting**: Allows CI tests and API jobs to bound work to a predictable runtime.
- **Deterministic maze expansion ordering**: Tie-breaking in the maze search queue is now fully deterministic, improving routing parity with v1.9 and making results reproducible.

## Infrastructure & Developer Experience

- **Java 25 and Gradle 9.4.1** (#614): The project now requires and builds with Java 25; CI runners updated accordingly. OpenRewrite migration recipes applied for Java 17 → 21 → 25.
- **Checkstyle** (Google Java Style) integrated into the build.
- **Multi-architecture Docker builds** (amd64 + arm64) with manual trigger support.
- **macOS arm64 CI builds** added (#614).
- **Website moved** from `/docs` to `/website`; GitHub Pages workflow updated.
- **DAC2020 benchmark suite** (10 KiCad designs) added to `fixtures/` with a PowerShell benchmarking script and documented results in `docs/Benchmarks.md`.
- **AGENTS.md** added: comprehensive project persona and guidelines for AI-assisted development.
- **Fanout feature removed** (#605): Simplifies the codebase; fanout routing was unused.
- **Snapshot and activity replay features removed** (#607): Legacy features cleaned up.
- **`WindowWelcome` and launch4j** removed as part of GUI initialization refactor.
- **KiCad 9 plugin compatibility fix**.

## What's Changed
* Fix issue 522 by @ceoloide in https://github.com/freerouting/freerouting/pull/541
* Avoid modifying collection while iterating over it (related to issue #491) by @ceoloide in https://github.com/freerouting/freerouting/pull/542
* Correctly update max value in Clearance-Matrix by @ceoloide in https://github.com/freerouting/freerouting/pull/543
* Fix race condition in StoppableThread by @ceoloide in https://github.com/freerouting/freerouting/pull/544
* Escape numerical padstack names (fixes #411) by @ceoloide in https://github.com/freerouting/freerouting/pull/548
* Fix potential memory leaks and reduce memory consumption by @ceoloide in https://github.com/freerouting/freerouting/pull/549
* Feat: add support for user-supplied random seed (fixes #545) by @ceoloide in https://github.com/freerouting/freerouting/pull/547
* Issue 555 performance regression by @andrasfuchs in https://github.com/freerouting/freerouting/pull/577
* Add DRC infrastructure with KiCad-compatible JSON output by @Copilot in https://github.com/freerouting/freerouting/pull/576
* Fix copper to edge clearance not respected on non-zero layers by @Copilot in https://github.com/freerouting/freerouting/pull/567
* OpenAPI 3.0 documentation and Swagger UI by @andrasfuchs in https://github.com/freerouting/freerouting/pull/587
* Add modular API key validation with Google Sheets provider by @andrasfuchs in https://github.com/freerouting/freerouting/pull/592
* KiCad compatible Design Rules Checker (DRC) with CLI support by @andrasfuchs in https://github.com/freerouting/freerouting/pull/601
* Progressed & Bugs Fixed & Remove old freerouting-laucher by @L1uTongweiNewAccount in https://github.com/freerouting/freerouting/pull/594

name: Freerouting v2.1.0
body:
This document outlines the key changes and improvements introduced in Freerouting version 2.1.0. This release focuses on providing better routing analysis through a new scoring system, significant algorithm refinements, a new Python client library, updated container support, and foundational work for future performance enhancements.

### New Scoring System Implementation

Version 2.1.0 introduces a comprehensive **scoring system** to offer objective metrics for evaluating autorouting results.

* **Quantitative Analysis:** The system provides detailed board statistics and calculates scores based on parameters like total trace length, via count, and route completion percentage.
* **Improved Feedback:** The underlying structure for board statistics has been significantly refactored to support this new system and facilitate comparison between different routing runs.
* **CLI Integration:** For command-line interface (CLI) usage, the routing job results, including input/output statistics and the calculated score, are now exported in JSON format upon completion, aiding automated workflows and analysis.

This feature aims to provide users with enhanced tools for assessing and optimizing routing outcomes.

### Algorithm Enhancements and Multi-threading Preparation

The core routing algorithms have undergone substantial refinement in this release, alongside preparatory work for multi-threaded operation:

* **Core Algorithm Improvements:**
    * **Backtracking Logic:** The capability to backtrack from difficult routing situations has been significantly improved, potentially increasing route completion rates.
    * **Hybrid Strategy:** A hybrid routing strategy is now employed more consistently to balance speed and result quality.
    * **Reliability Fixes:** Issues such as potential infinite loops in specific modes have been addressed, and prior improvement thresholds have been removed for more consistent behavior.
    * **Shape Support:** Support for simplex shapes within the 45-degree routing algorithm has been added.
* **Multi-threading Prepared (Not Enabled by Default):**
    * Significant code changes have been implemented to prepare the router for multi-threaded execution. This includes making core data structures like `BoardHistory` thread-safe.
    * **Important:** This multi-threading capability is **not enabled by default** in version 2.1.0. It requires further testing and bugfixing before being activated in a future release. The groundwork laid in 2.1.0 facilitates this future development and allows for experimental use.
* **Optimizer Availability:** The optimizer functionality has been made GUI-independent and re-enabled for API and CLI execution paths.
* **Enhanced Logging:** More detailed feedback is provided during routing and optimization, offering better insight into the process and potential failure points.

These changes collectively aim to improve routing reliability and quality, while paving the way for future performance scaling.

### New Python Client Library

To facilitate integration and scripting for Python users, a new **Freerouting Python Client library** has been introduced. It is available in its own dedicated repository: [https://github.com/freerouting/freerouting-python-client](https://github.com/freerouting/freerouting-python-client)

I encourage Python developers utilizing Freerouting in their workflows to explore this new library. 
You can start using it by simply installing the `freerouting-client` package:

```bash
pip install freerouting-client
```

### Docker Image Updates on GitHub Container Registry (GHCR)

The process for distributing Freerouting via Docker has been updated:

* **Automated Publication:** GitHub Actions workflows are now configured to automatically build and publish Docker images to the GitHub Container Registry (GHCR).
* **Stable and Nightly Builds:** Users can now access Docker images for both stable releases (e.g., `2.1.0`) and development (nightly) builds directly from `ghcr.io/freerouting/freerouting`.

This provides a standardized and accessible method for obtaining Freerouting versions in containerized environments.

### A Note on Project Stewardship

This release also marks a transition in the project's maintenance. As the sole developer and maintainer, Andras Fuchs will be stepping back from active development leadership following this release.

Developing and maintaining Freerouting demands significant time and resources, exemplified by the 61 hours invested in this release alone, a much more in the last 5 years. While the project has benefited from community usage and bug reporting, the level of direct code contribution and financial sponsorship required for sustainable, long-term development by a single maintainer has proven challenging to achieve.

Gratitude is extended to all users and contributors who have engaged with the project. To ensure Freerouting's continued development and availability, future support through institutional backing (e.g., from a company, foundation, or university) is being sought. name: Freerouting v2.0.0
body:
This is one of the biggest updates in Freerouting's history! I’ve volunteered 220 hours into this release, and I truly hope you enjoy it!

What’s new? A lot! Let’s dive in:

### GUI Upgrade

![GUI screenshot](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fbee550e-f876-4a33-bcbc-cfbdd8f28b2c)

In v1.9, I introduced anonymous telemetry, which helped me understand which features users rely on most. Based on that data, I’ve revamped the user interface, making it sleeker and more modern. A few features (like context-aware help, select mode, macros, and snapshot management) have been disabled and will be fully removed in future releases.

* Menus have been rearranged and simplified for better usability.
* New icons, mode selectors, and unit controls have been added.
* Several router settings windows have been combined, and I plan to streamline them even further based on what settings are actually used.
* Warnings and error indicators have been modernized and are now displayed in the bottom right corner.
* A new User Settings window allows you to configure telemetry and contact preferences.
* Freerouting now has a refreshed color palette that aligns with KiCad’s modern look. While the palette remains customizable, the color editor will be removed in the next release.

### Configuration framework

A brand-new configuration framework unifies how users set preferences. Now, you can choose from multiple methods: `freerouting.json` configuration file, environment variables, command line arguments, or GUI.

* Configuration file: Modify the `freerouting.json` file directly.
* Environment variables: Override configuration settings with variables in the format FREEROUTING__{key}__{subkey}. For example, FREEROUTING__ROUTER__MAX_PASSES=20 changes the maximum passes to 20.
* Command line arguments: Adjust settings like --router.max_passes=10 to control the number of allowed passes.
* GUI: If enabled, certain settings can be tweaked directly through the interface.

Check out [its documentation](https://github.com/freerouting/freerouting/blob/master/docs/settings.md) for more details.

### Improved Localization

Localization has been overhauled. Previously, short text fragments were combined programmatically, which caused issues with non-English languages. Now, we use whole sentence templates with placeholders, offering more flexibility for translators. For example, `"Saving Specctra session '{{filename}}' was successful."` gives more control to translators, ensuring better results for all languages.

Additionally, I've added fallback mechanisms and generalized support for labels, buttons, and text boxes across the entire UI.

### Routing job scheduler

I introduced a multi-threaded routing job scheduler. It is responsible for managing and executing the routing jobs of Freerouting. This improvement enables us to run routing jobs in parallel. This was a crucial prerequisite for the API to work, but it will also let GUI users run and monitor long-running jobs in the background.

### Public API (beta)

The **Freerouting API** is now publicly available at [https://api.freerouting.app/v1](https://api.freerouting.app/v1/system/status). This involved a huge backend refactor and opens the door to tighter integration with EDAs like KiCad, EasyEDA, and tscircuit.

The API and [its documentation](https://github.com/freerouting/freerouting/blob/master/docs/API_v1.md) are still evolving, with close collaboration from the tscircuit team to make it as useful as possible.

### CLI interface

Freerouting now natively supports headless operation, allowing you to access its functionality via the command line, without needing a graphical interface. You can run Freerouting in CLI mode by setting the `gui.enabled` setting to `false`.

### Unit Tests

I’ve introduced unit testing for evaluating DSN files before accepting new commits. This helps ensure new features or contributions don’t introduce bugs. It supports testing in local environments, via GitHub Actions, and Docker.

### Docker support

Freerouting now supports Docker! The container is compatible with both ARM64 and x64 platforms, and it works on Microsoft Azure.

### Personal notes

I know release notes are usually impersonal, but we’re all geeks here, so let me get a bit personal. :) I love Freerouting because it gives time back to people who love to build. When it works, it’s amazing. But sometimes it doesn’t, and I know the frustration that comes with it.

I work hard to make it better, but sometimes other projects, or life gets in the way. Being an open-source maintainer isn’t easy—issues pile up, and there’s never enough time. It's a race that never ends, and it’s both exhilarating and exhausting.

I’ll be taking a short break for a few months, but I’ll be back. Please continue to post issues and pull requests, and I’ll get to them as soon as I can.

## Sponsors

A heartfelt thank you to my sponsors for their invaluable support and motivation, which enables me to continue volunteering as the sole developer and maintainer of Freerouting.

Special thanks to @tscircuit (and @seveibar) for your ongoing generosity!

I’d also like to acknowledge past sponsors: @cpyne, @rozza-m, and @digilent. Your support has been essential to this project.

Last but definitely not least, I'd like to thank my family for tirelessly accepting that when I said, "Just another 5 minutes for this quick fix," it often meant they'd see me hours later. Their patience as they waited again and again for me to finish up and join them is truly heroic. Hearts to my lovely wife—you kept me alive with fantastic food despite my best efforts to subsist solely on caffeine and code during those intense programming marathons.

Since I’m currently the only active contributor to Freerouting, even a small monthly contribution would be greatly appreciated. If you’d like to support this project, please consider sponsoring me: [GitHub Sponsors](https://github.com/sponsors/andrasfuchs). Thank you!

Many things improved since the last release including [bug fixes and improvements](https://github.com/freerouting/freerouting/milestone/5?closed=1), and I would like to highlight just a few:

### Global settings file (freerouting.json)
We now have a global `freerouting.json` file stored in the temp folder for all the defaults that we use. They don't cover all the settings we have just yet, but you can still have more control over the processes than before. Command line arguments can override them, just like before. Freerouting now can remember your the default folder from where you opened your last board, yay!

### Modern, KiCad-like color schema
The color schema was modified to match KiCad good-looking, more modern look:
![image](https://github.com/freerouting/freerouting/assets/910321/7e396aaf-8264-4a88-a215-4b9e1e8f6737)

### Analytics
Added Segment's Analytics framework to the code, so we finally can get insights from anonymous usage statistics. This is a crucial step moving forward, because the plan is to have a feature reduction release in the near future, where we can get rid of all the functions that are not used by you. You can disable this by using the `-da` command line argument.

We fixed a few issues with keepouts, component rotation and snapshot files, added more robust 2+ layer support, automated version checking, new dialog boxes (with `-dct` command line argument to set the timeout), fixed high DPI texts, fixed KiCad plugin issues (including on-demand JRE installation) and compile time warnings.

name: Freerouting v1.6.0
body:
This release have a new feature that allows users to tell autorouter to skip a net-class. This can be useful for example if you want to manually connect components to GND, VCC after freerouting finished. You have this option in the GUI in the Rules / Net Classes / "ignore by autorouter" column, or you can use the new "-inc" command line argument to set those net classes. E.g. `-inc GND,VCC` tells the autorouter to not route the connections in the GND and VCC net classes.

The autorouter parameters were slightly modified to improve the end results. It causes the algorithm to run a little longer, but our tests confirmed that it is a reasonable tradeoff. To run the autorouter indefinitely, use the `-oit 0` command line argument.

We moved from Java 11 to Java 17.

DSN file reader was upgraded to handle non-ANSI (Cyrillic, Chinese, etc.) characters.

From this release on macOS installer package is not supported. Freerouting still works on macOS by using the .jar release, but it needs a Java 17 runtime to be installed. If someone who 1, has a Mac and 2, is a member of the [Apple Developer Program](https://developer.apple.com/programs/) has the time to work on the macOS installer, let me know.

As always, this release contains many small fixes and improvements.

body:
This release contains improvements and bug fixes, including language detection and Chinese translations, multi-threading locking issue fix, KiCad plugin update, and package updates. Please note that our KiCad plugin update is still waiting for approval from the owner of [its repo](https://github.com/random-builder/kicad_freerouting-plugin/pull/12).

With this release we have performance improvements too, including the multi-threading route optimizer and its fine-tuned settings that can lead to huge time savings. The tuned values are based on test data, detailed [here](https://github.com/freerouting/freerouting#multi-threaded-implementation-of-routing-optimization).

We have a few new command line parameters:
* -oit [percentage]: stops the route optimizer if the improvement drops below a certain percentage threshold per pass. Default is 0.1%, and 0% means to continue improving until there are no more route options to test.
* -im: saves intermediate steps in version-specific binary format. This allows to user to resume the interrupted optimization from the last checkpoint. Turned off by default.
* -h: shows help.
